claims.claim: Copilot cloud-agent internet access is limited by a firewall that operates only inside the GitHub Actions appliance, only on processes started via the agent's Bash tool, and is configured from GitHub organization/repository Internet-access settings that an organization can lock so repositories cannot override.

source_lineage.quote: Only applies within the {% data variables.product.prodname_actions %} appliance
Only applies within the GitHub Actions appliance

claims.strongest_caveat: The same docs disclose that the firewall does not apply to MCP servers or copilot-setup-steps processes, and that sophisticated attacks may bypass it; it is not a comprehensive security boundary.

claims.claim: Repository administrators can toggle Enable firewall only when the organization-level setting is Let repositories decide; if the org sets Enabled or Disabled, individual repositories cannot change it.

source_lineage.quote: If the organization-level setting is **Enabled** or **Disabled**, you can't change this setting for individual repositories.
If the organization-level setting is Enabled or Disabled, you can't change this setting for individual repositories.

claims.strongest_caveat: This lock is documented for GitHub.com settings; this unit did not exercise a live org-admin UI, so the lock is graded from docs+API source, not from a runtime org mutation.

claims.claim: Cloud-agent MCP servers are configured by pasting JSON into the repository settings MCP servers page on GitHub.com and clicking Save MCP configuration; the JSON is not the committed .github/mcp.json used by Copilot CLI.

source_lineage.quote: You enter the JSON configuration directly into the settings for the repository on {% data variables.product.prodname_dotcom_the_website %}.
You enter the JSON configuration directly into the settings for the repository on GitHub.com.

claims.strongest_caveat: The JSON object shape (mcpServers, type, tools, command/url) is intentionally similar to VS Code/CLI configs; similarity of schema is not identity of enforcement. Adapting .vscode/mcp.json still requires adding a tools key and dropping inputs/envFile.

claims.claim: Copilot cloud agent and Copilot code review only support MCP tools (not resources or prompts) and do not currently support remote MCP servers that use OAuth.

source_lineage.quote: do not currently support remote MCP servers that leverage OAuth
do not currently support remote MCP servers that leverage OAuth

claims.strongest_caveat: This is a product limitation of the hosted agent, not a property of MCP itself; a local Copilot CLI session may speak OAuth/HTTP MCP that the cloud agent will refuse.

claims.claim: `.github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml` is picked up only when the job is named copilot-setup-steps; only steps, permissions, runs-on, services, snapshot, and timeout-minutes (max 59) may be customized, and any other job settings are ignored. fetch-depth on actions/checkout is overridden by the agent.

source_lineage.quote: If you try to customize other settings, your changes will be ignored.
If you try to customize other settings, your changes will be ignored.

claims.strongest_caveat: The YAML file itself is an ordinary Actions workflow and can be copied into another repo, but the ignore/override behavior is applied by GitHub's cloud-agent runner, not by Actions YAML semantics. Self-hosted runners additionally require the integrated firewall to be disabled or the agent is blocked.

claims.claim: Repository-wide custom instructions are a Markdown file at `.github/copilot-instructions.md`. The file is used in practice (microsoft/vscode ships one) and is loaded as prompt context by both Copilot cloud agent and Copilot CLI; it is not a server-side admission gate.

source_lineage.quote: VS Code Copilot Instructions
VS Code Copilot Instructions

claims.strongest_caveat: Loading the file is product-specific (Copilot discovers a named path). The bytes are portable; Copilot's interpretation and whitespace-collapsing rules are not a portable runtime contract. Path-specific `*.instructions.md` files use applyTo matching on CLI.

claims.claim: Official docs specify repository-wide instructions as `copilot-instructions.md` in the `.github` directory, plus path-specific `NAME.instructions.md` under `.github/instructions`.

source_lineage.quote: These are specified in a `copilot-instructions.md` file in the `.github` directory of the repository.
These are specified in a copilot-instructions.md file in the .github directory of the repository.

claims.strongest_caveat: Docs also mention AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / GEMINI.md as agent instruction files; support differs by surface (see custom instructions support matrix).

claims.claim: Organization custom instructions are entered in the organization Copilot Custom instructions settings text box and saved there; they are not a repository file.

source_lineage.quote: You can add organization custom instructions via your organization settings.
You can add organization custom instructions via your organization settings.

claims.strongest_caveat: This unit did not capture a live org-settings payload (would require org-admin credentials). Classification is from official how-to prose plus the Contents API source of that how-to.

claims.claim: Copilot CLI `--allow-tool` and `--deny-tool` apply only to the current session and are not written to ~/.copilot/permissions-config.json; deny rules still beat allow rules and saved approvals.

source_lineage.quote: Command-line options such as `--allow-tool` and `--deny-tool` apply only to the current session and aren't written to `permissions-config.json`.
Command-line options such as --allow-tool and --deny-tool apply only to the current session and aren't written to permissions-config.json.

claims.strongest_caveat: Interactive 'don't ask again in this repo' approvals ARE persisted in permissions-config.json; that persistence is still a local file, not GitHub-hosted enforcement. MDM/server-managed permissions are a separate server-enforced overlay (C-CLI-MDM).

claims.claim: Copilot CLI loads MDM managed settings and server-managed settings at startup; MDM wins per key, long-running sessions re-fetch hourly, and keys such as allowedMcpServers / deniedMcpServers / permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode are admin-enforced. An MDM value of disable for disableBypassPermissionsMode always wins.

source_lineage.quote: {% data variables.copilot.copilot_cli_short %} also loads server-managed settings at startup, in addition to MDM.
Copilot CLI also loads server-managed settings at startup, in addition to MDM.

claims.strongest_caveat: File-based MDM paths (/etc/github-copilot/managed-settings.json on Linux) are local files, but they are a device-policy channel, not user config. This unit did not receive a live MDM payload.

claims.claim: Cloud agent receives only Agents secrets/variables. Actions, Codespaces, and Dependabot secrets are not passed. MCP config can see only names prefixed COPILOT_MCP_.

source_lineage.quote: {% data variables.copilot.copilot_cloud_agent %} does not have access to {% data variables.product.prodname_actions %}, {% data variables.product.prodname_codespaces %}, or {% data variables.product.prodname_dependabot %} secrets and variables. Only Agents secrets and variables are passed to the agent.
Copilot cloud agent does not have access to GitHub Actions, Codespaces, or Dependabot secrets and variables. Only Agents secrets and variables are passed to the agent.

claims.strongest_caveat: A local CLI process sees the operator's shell environment instead; copying COPILOT_MCP_* names into a laptop env is not the same control as GitHub Agents secrets.

claims.claim: The organization policy 'Copilot can search the web' does not apply to Copilot cloud agent even though the cloud agent can access the Internet; assuming that policy is portable across surfaces is a documented error.

source_lineage.quote: {% data variables.copilot.copilot_cloud_agent %} **can** access the Internet, but the "{% data variables.product.prodname_copilot_short %} can search the web" policy does not affect this capability.
Copilot cloud agent can access the Internet, but the "Copilot can search the web" policy does not affect this capability.

claims.strongest_caveat: The policy matrix uses octicons rather than the words true/false; this claim quotes the explicit prose note, not an inferred table cell. Egress is separately gated by the appliance firewall (C-FW-APPLIANCE).

claims.claim: Copilot CLI MCP servers are configured in local files (~/.copilot/mcp-config.json, .mcp.json, .github/mcp.json) or via `copilot mcp add`; project files closer to cwd win. This is a client-local loader, distinct from GitHub.com repository MCP settings.

source_lineage.quote: The server is added to the user configuration at `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`.
The server is added to the user configuration at ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json.

claims.strongest_caveat: If the org/enterprise has configured a registry URL and allowlist policy, those settings apply to Copilot CLI and only permitted servers can run — an admin overlay on top of the local files.

claims.claim: Custom agent profiles are Markdown files with YAML frontmatter (tools, mcp-servers, target). argument-hint and handoffs from VS Code agent files are ignored on github.com cloud agent; mcp-servers is not used in VS Code IDE custom agents.

source_lineage.quote: They are ignored to ensure compatibility.
They are ignored to ensure compatibility.

claims.strongest_caveat: Unrecognized tool names are ignored by design so product-specific tools can be listed without breaking other surfaces. File format is portable; ignored-field behavior is not.

claims.claim: Starting a cloud-agent task via POST /agents/repos/{owner}/{repo}/tasks is a GitHub-hosted API that accepts only user-to-server tokens; GitHub App installation (server-to-server) tokens are not supported.

source_lineage.quote: Server-to-server tokens, such as {% data variables.product.prodname_github_app %} installation access tokens, are not supported.
Server-to-server tokens, such as GitHub App installation access tokens, are not supported.

claims.strongest_caveat: The API is documented as public preview and subject to change. A local Copilot CLI session is not this API.

control_table.justification: Docs state the firewall only operates within the GitHub Actions appliance and is toggled from GitHub Internet-access settings; there is no Copilot CLI equivalent. Org can lock the toggle.
Allowlist entries are stored in org/repo Internet-access settings; org custom allowlist items cannot be deleted at repository level. Applied by the hosted appliance, not by a local process.

control_table.control_name: Repository MCP JSON stored in GitHub.com settings
control_table.justification: Administrators paste JSON into repository settings and Save MCP configuration; GitHub validates syntax server-side and the hosted agent starts those servers autonomously without approval prompts.
The object keys are shared with Copilot CLI and VS Code, so the file shape can be copied; cloud agent still requires a tools key and rejects OAuth remotes that a local client may accept.

control_table.control_name: Cloud-agent MCP: tools only, no OAuth remotes
control_table.justification: Official how-to states cloud agent/code review do not support MCP resources/prompts or OAuth remote servers. That refusal is in the hosted runtime, not in the JSON file.
Wrong job name is not picked up; extra job keys are ignored; checkout fetch-depth is overridden. Those behaviors are the hosted agent's, not portable Actions semantics.

These are committed Markdown files loaded as prompt context. microsoft/vscode publishes a live .github/copilot-instructions.md. Copilot CLI also discovers the same paths. No GitHub admission API is required for the file to exist.
Org owners type instructions into organization Copilot settings and Save changes. There is no repo file to copy into a local runtime.
Flags apply only to the current local session and are not written to permissions-config.json. Enforcement is the local CLI process.
The CLI walks from cwd to repo root loading local JSON files; user-level ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json is a laptop file. Distinct from GitHub.com MCP settings.

control_table.control_name: CLI MDM and server-managed settings (allowedMcpServers, disableBypass)
control_table.justification: CLI re-fetches server-managed settings hourly; MDM disableBypassPermissionsMode=disable always wins and cannot be overridden by account switch. allowedMcpServers empty array is deny-all.
Only the Agents secret type is injected; Actions/Codespaces/Dependabot secrets are withheld. MCP sees only COPILOT_MCP_* names.

control_table.control_name: Org policy 'Copilot can search the web'
control_table.justification: GitHub's policy matrix note states cloud agent can access the Internet but this policy does not affect that capability. Treating the IDE/chat policy as binding the coding agent is the portability error.
Profiles are files under .github/agents, so the document is portable; github.com ignores argument-hint/handoffs and VS Code ignores mcp-servers. Ignore lists are product-enforced.
Task creation is a GitHub REST endpoint that rejects installation tokens. A local runtime cannot host this control.

question: What customization contract does the Copilot coding agent expose (instructions files, allowed tools, MCP configuration, firewall policy), and which parts are enforced server-side and therefore not portable to a local runtime?
residual_unknowns: Live org-admin mutation of Enable firewall was not executed (no org).
GitHub code search for copilot-setup-steps.yml returned HTTP 401 unauthenticated.

reviewer.method: Adversarial refuter defaults to REFUTED on single-rail or all-client-side tables; surviving claims keep strongest_caveat.

schema_gate.note: Shared research-claim-record.schema.json is not on disk (RES-0001). This unit validates against a local discriminator that rejects garbage, single-rail claims, and an unjustified control table.

sentinel: SUCCESS:RES-0026 in the receipt AND a control table with a client-vs-server enforcement column justified per row

tests.detail: control_table has client_vs_server_enforcement and a >=24 char justification on every row
SERVER-ENFORCED count is >= 1; all-client mutant is rejected by probe2
every claim is E2 with structured-api + prose-source on distinct hosts
portable_to_local_runtime is false on every SERVER-ENFORCED row
